summary: Independent review of Webull OCO reconciliation before managed exits, re-reviewed from scratch at the corrected head. THE BLOCKER I RAISED ON 3a9458d4 IS FIXED AND I VERIFIED IT THE SAME WAY I FOUND IT. On the earlier head the hold sat at the top of _emit_v2_managed_sell, the single emit point for every v2 software exit (CW_TARGET/CW_FLOOR/CW_HARD_STOP/CW_FLIP all reach it via _emit_v2_exit_on_loop), so an unreadable pair suppressed the hard stop as well as the redundant close; I demonstrated it with a position at entry 10.00, hard stop trigger 9.50, bid forced to 8.00 (minus 20 percent) over five evaluation cycles on both 'unanswerable' and 'reserved' — zero broker submissions, zero sell intents, warning only. Re-running that identical test at c55f3f1f now shows the sell reaching the broker with reason=oms_v2_managed_exit:HARD_STOP, both outcomes. The fix classifies the reason: _is_protective_v2_exit gates the hold, protective exits continue, a broker-filled pair still suppresses the redundant sell, and profit-taking (CW_TARGET, SCALE_) is still held — I independently grepped every emitted managed-exit reason and the classification table covers all of them. My second finding is also fixed: a throttled unreadable result now returns the remembered outcome instead of manufacturing 'reserved', so absence of evidence is no longer turned into positive evidence that protection survived. A terminal branch now exists, bounded by the existing _V2_EXIT_ABANDON_AFTER_FAILURES budget rather than a second retry loop, with V2_OVERNIGHT_FLATTEN terminal immediately, and INC1 is kept open until the pair positively reports release or a fill — terminal never means released. Mutations, each independently RED against tests/unit/test_v2_managed_exit.py + test_exit_reservation_release.py + test_webull_adapter.py (142 passed baseline): protective=False at all three call sites -> 4 failed AND the suppression reproduces behaviourally; CW_HARD_STOP removed from the protective set -> 1; throttle returns 'reserved' -> 1; terminal cap removed -> 1; resolved_by_fill no longer suppresses -> 2; everything protective -> 2. NOTE ON MY OWN METHOD: my first attempt at the protective mutation hit only one of the three call sites and appeared to survive; that was an incomplete mutation, not a control gap, and the corrected all-sites mutation is red. Controlled full unit pair vs base 4fed979: base 46 failed/3540 passed, head 46 failed/3574 passed, ZERO new failure names and ZERO fixed. Ruff clean. Ancestor test PASS. Trial-merged against #944 (both touch oms/service.py) and #945 — clean. Scope note carried forward for the operator: adapters without release_exit_pair_for_close return 'unsupported', which is not in the suppressing set, so Schwab and simulated paths are unchanged and the behaviour is Webull-only. RESIDUAL, NOT BLOCKING: _PROTECTIVE_V2_EXIT_REASONS is a hand-maintained enumeration and a future protective reason added to the code would default to held; a completeness assertion tying the table to the reasons actually emitted in src would close that.
